research_rationale:
EO 9052 (February 6, 1942, Franklin D. Roosevelt) is a short order read in full in the held Federal Register text (issue of Tuesday, February 10, 1942). Its only operative command amends Subdivision VIII of Schedule A of the Civil Service Rules; the amendment is the addition of a paragraph numbered 30 naming "The Solicitor of the Department of" the Interior. Part III of EO 9830 (signed February 24, 1947; 12 FR 1259, issue of Tuesday, February 25, 1947) is the sentence "hereby revoked:" followed by a list of orders by number, and its enacting clause reads "effective May 1, 1947:" for all Parts alike. The list includes the row "No. 9052 of February 6, 1942.", so EO 9830 expressly revokes this order, and the order's own text states no period, condition or end date. The held EO 9830 text has no wording that saves or excepts any listed order. The first end is the express revocation, effective May 1, 1947.
